newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan April long-term prime seen unchanged at 2.5%.
newsitem.headline: Japan April long-term prime seen unchanged at 2.5%.

text.p: Japan's long-term prime lending rate for April is likely to be set at 2.5 percent, unchanged from the previous month, sources at long-term credit banks said on Monday.
The Industrial Bank of Japan Ltd (IBJ) is expected to announce its April long-term prime rate on Tuesday.
"Judging from current market conditions, the long-term prime rate is highly likely to be left unchanged in April," said a source at one long-term credit bank.
The prime rate, that at which long-term credit banks lend to their most creditworthy customers, is customarily set 0.9 percentage point above the coupon rate of the benchmark IBJ five-year debenture.
The IBJ's 1.6 percent five-year bank debenture issued in March was traded at a yield of around 1.70 percent on Monday, up from 1.63 percent last Friday, bond traders said.
The IBJ customarily changes the coupon rate for its new debentures when market yields of the previous month's debentures deviate more than 0.2 percentage point from the coupon.
Bank debentures were weaker on Monday despite a rally in the Japanese government bond (JGB) market.
"Investors are becoming more risk-conscious. They are shunning bank debentures in favour of JGBs," said a trader at a brokerage house.
"The April long-term prime rate will be decided after seeing how bank debentures trade in the secondary market on Tuesday," said another source at long-term credit banks.
The long-term prime rate was last cut in December to a record-low 2.5 percent from 2.7 percent in November.

Two other long-term credit banks - Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan Ltd (LTCB) and Nippon Credit Bank Ltd (NCB) - are expected to announce the coupon rates for their April five-year debentures on Wednesday.
